doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Being a father during the New York studio years
summary: With four kids in school, he was home every night during twelve years of studio work.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I see. What was it like trying to be a father and—

Well that was a hard thing to do. But in those days all my kids were going to school, four of them, and I’d see them in the morning and I’d see them on the weekends, because there was nothing going on on the weekends, although there were some record dates, recording sessions, special occasions we had to go in and do. But luckily they were all going to school and I saw them as much as I could. But I used to take them into New York too to see some of the sessions, whenever they were off, in the summertime and all that. And it was that I was home every night that was the most important thing I think. That I always came home. I was in New York for like twelve years doing that kind of work.
So in one sense you were home more regularly than going on the road.
Oh that was the most I’ve ever been home was that little stretch there.
